sample.title: How China’s Export Machine Is Beating Tariffs
sample.description:
Tariffs and trade barriers thrown up by the US and Europe were supposed to slow China’s export machine. Instead, it has accelerated. China’s trade surplus this year is on track to exceed the $1.2 trillion record set in 2025.

While China’s exports to the West dropped between 2024 and 2025, its exports to Southeast Asia, South and Central America, Africa, Japan and South Korea all increased. And it’s not only about finding new markets abroad: China also has moved up the value chain. The country is now a major force in everything from electric cars and solar panels to robots and artificial intelligence.

But China’s export boom is unfolding against a fragile domestic backdrop. The country continues to grapple with weak consumer demand, a prolonged property downturn and high youth unemployment, making exports an increasingly important source of growth.

sample.description:
Emily Chang travels to Paris, Seoul and Los Angeles to explore Netflix's next chapter in the entertainment world. In conversations with Co-CEO Ted Sarandos and Hollywood stars Ben Affleck and Lily Collins, Chang probes the company's global strategy, AI ambitions and executive shakeups.

Netflix’s Sarandos Says the Streaming TV Wars Are Just Beginning: https://bloom.bg/4AIsmDK

Netflix Inc. Co-Chief Executive Officer Ted Sarandos believes the streaming TV wars are far from over, as the industry he helped create enters a more mature and competitive phase.

“No one has won the streaming wars,” Sarandos said in an interview on Bloomberg’s The Circuit with Emily Chang. “The streaming wars are continuing as we go.” With less than half of US television viewing going to services like his, “we’re still in the very early innings of this,” he said.

sample.title: How the killer of a 12-year-old was finally put behind bars | BBC News
sample.description:
A 12-year-old boy is killed by a speeding driver. What follows is a two-year fight for justice by his family. 

Keaton Slater died in the collision on Coventry’s Radford Road on June 14, 2024. His death unites the city and spurs his family to do all they can to ensure his killer is put behind bars.

But Aleksanders Dolars evaded capture for more than two years by fleeing to Latvia. 

He was finally brought to justice following a determined campaign by Keaton’s parents Louise and Clint. But even after sentencing, the family’s fight is not over.
